questions.cardText:
[Cultural Studies] Which of the following countries has a calendar with 13 months?
A. Ethiopian
B. Brunei
C. Japan
Answer: A. This is because the Ethiopian calendar calculates the birth year of Jesus Christ differently. When the Catholic Church updated its calculation around 500 CE, the Ethiopian Orthodox Church did not.
questions.de: Der Kalender welches Landes hat 13 Monate – zwölf zu je 30 Tagen und einen kurzen dreizehnten Monat mit fünf oder sechs Tagen?
questions.en: Which country's calendar has 13 months – twelve of 30 days plus a short thirteenth month of five or six days?

timeline.labelEn: Ethiopia celebrates the start of the year 2000 in its own calendar, the Ethiopian Millennium
timeline.labelDe: Äthiopien feiert den Beginn des Jahres 2000 seines eigenen Kalenders, das äthiopische Millennium

questions.notes: Card's option reads 'Ethiopian' (an adjective) for a country. Its explanation is wrong for the question: the different dating of Christ's incarnation (Annianus c. 400 vs Dionysius Exiguus 525) explains why Ethiopian years run 7–8 years behind, not why there are 13 months; the 13th month (Pagume) is the 5–6 epagomenal days after twelve 30-day months (Wikipedia).

questions.cardText:
[Astronomy] What is the “Panspermia theory”?
A. It explains the movement of galaxies
B. It suggests life on Earth came from outer space
C. It describes the formation of stars
Answer: B. Panspermia hypothesizes that life on Earth may have originated from microorganisms or organic particles from space, possibly carried by cosmic bodies.
questions.de: Welche Hypothese besagt, dass das Leben auf der Erde aus dem Weltall stammt – als Mikroorganismen oder organische Teilchen, die von Himmelskörpern hergebracht wurden?
questions.en: Which hypothesis proposes that life on Earth came from outer space, as microorganisms or organic particles carried here by cosmic bodies?

timeline.labelEn: The idea of panspermia is traced back to the Greek philosopher Anaxagoras in the 5th century BC
timeline.labelDe: Die Idee der Panspermie geht auf den griechischen Philosophen Anaxagoras im 5. Jahrhundert v. Chr. zurück

questions.notes: Reversed from 'what is panspermia' to ask the name. Panspermia remains a fringe hypothesis, not established theory.
